title: Chirped Depth-Graded Stack for Broadened UV Reflection Band
scientific_hypothesis: A depth-graded stack where bilayer thickness increases from air toward substrate will broaden the UV reflection band beyond what a periodic stack achieves, while maintaining SWIR transmission by keeping longer-period layers deeper in the stack.
design_principle: Depth-graded multilayers (L24) use varying bilayer thickness to create constructive interference across a broader wavelength range. Thinner bilayers near the air interface reflect shorter wavelengths; thicker bilayers deeper in the stack reflect longer wavelengths within the UV band, collectively broadening the reflection band.
proposed_topology: Air | 15 bilayers of (HfO2 | SiO2) with thickness increasing from air to substrate | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: bilayer thickness gradient parameter (rate of thickness increase per bilayer)
base bilayer thickness at air interface
maximum bilayer thickness at substrate interface
soft_objectives: maximize mean reflectance across full 300-450 nm band (not just center)
maintain mean transmittance above 90% in 1000-1700 nm band
minimize thickness gradient to reduce fabrication complexity
manufacturing_considerations: thickness gradient must be monotonic for fabrication reproducibility
L08 demonstrates HfO2 deposition control in multilayer structures
theory_basis: Depth-graded multilayer theory for broadband reflection (L24)
L39 demonstrates wideband dichroic coating fabrication using graded approaches
expected_advantages: Broader reflection bandwidth than periodic stack
L24 shows depth-graded coatings achieve high reflectivity across wide spectral ranges
Better tolerance to wavelength shift from angle variation
known_risks: Graded stacks require more precise thickness control during deposition
May introduce more absorption if HfO2 layers become too thick
L26 notes defect formation in HfO2 films can affect optical properties
execution_request_english: Design a chirped multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. The stack consists of 30 layers: 15 bilayers of alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. Bilayer thickness increases monotonically from air interface to substrate interface. Optimize three parameters: base bilayer thickness at air side, thickness increment per bilayer, and maximum bilayer thickness at substrate side. Maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band while maximizing transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band. Total layer count is exactly 30. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only.
